# OmniVibe Consumer — The Promise the Store Could Not Keep
> **GitHub-first narrative · GICS04 · 2026-10-19.** Fictional educational case. GitHub is canonical; Notion is the KM hub. Original research and13 HR child-page references remain below. New names, incidents, options and consumer-stream designs are illustrative. Unattended synchronization is unverified.
**Start here:** [Executive One-Pager](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/executive-one-pager.md) · [Hero Story](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/hero-story.md) · [22-Section Master](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/master/README.md) · [16 Personas](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md) · [12 Simulations](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/simulations/README.md) · [Seven Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [Resources](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/resources/README.md)
## Prologue — A disconnected promise
An invented customer arrives for a collection the app marked ready. The store cannot reconcile the promise; a new associate is also waiting for access and training. These events are discovery triggers, not historical evidence or a proven causal diagnosis.
## Act I — Understand the Enterprise (OVC-M01–04)
Fictional CEO **Maya Sterling (OVC-P01)** leads a source-stipulated **USD 28B** consumer group with **72,000 employees across 48 countries**, headquartered in London and Singapore.
Source revenue mix: fashion/lifestyle 32%, beauty 18%, home 17%, specialty retail 15%, travel/experiences 10%, digital marketplace 8%. Source assets include3,200 owned/franchise stores,14 e-commerce sites,26 DCs,140 micro-fulfillment locations and3,800 suppliers/partners.
Most source architecture detail addresses fragmented workforce data, journeys, portals and integrations. Customer/fulfillment incidents and designs below are labelled extensions.
[Enterprise theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/master/theme-a-enterprise.md)
## Act II — Choose the Future (OVC-M05–08)
Brand chief **Elena Rossi (OVC-P03)** values distinct experiences. CFO **Adrian Tan (OVC-P02)** demands evidence before funding. CHRO **Ravi Kapoor (OVC-P04)** connects workforce readiness to business outcomes.
Compare brand-local pilots, central platform first and federated journey experiments with common data/privacy/integration standards. The third is provisional.
**No investment budget, financial return or quantified KPI targets are supplied.** These remain TBD.
[Strategy theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/master/theme-b-strategy.md)
## Act III — Architect One Connected Workforce (OVC-M09–12)
The source 13 journeys connect foundation, acquisition, onboarding, performance, development, rewards, learning, payroll, time, analytics, experience, AI and integration.
Architect **Priya Shah (OVC-P11)** and integration lead **Jonas Lim (OVC-P12)** trace capabilities and data contracts. **Farah Ahmed (OVC-P13)** challenges unjustified data sharing.
Source SAP proposals include SuccessFactors modules, Work Zone, People Analytics, Joule and BTP/Integration Suite. Current capability, licensing and localization require verification. Illustrative consumer streams include Discover-to-Purchase, Promise-to-Fulfill, Return-to-Resolution, Trend-to-Assortment and Skill-to-Service-Readiness.
[Architecture theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/master/theme-c-architecture.md)
## Act IV — Sequence and Fund Learning (OVC-M13–16)
Preserve the four source waves:
1. Foundation: HR01,HR07,HR08,HR12.
2. Talent lifecycle: HR02a,HR02b,HR03,HR04.
3. Capability/rewards: HR05,HR06.
4. Intelligence/experience: HR09,HR10,HR11.
Dates and durations are absent. Pilot costs, baseline collection and measurable benefit hypotheses precede enterprise funding. No borrowed sector budget or guaranteed ROI is introduced.
[Transformation theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/master/theme-d-transformation.md)
## Act V — Make Change Work in the Shift (OVC-M17–19)
Payroll director **Nadia Rahman (OVC-P05)** requires reconciliation. Store director **Oliver Brooks (OVC-P06)** and associate **Nikhil Das (OVC-P16)** test practical access and learning. Skills lead **Aisha Okafor (OVC-P09)** asks what employees can demonstrate after practice.
A bounded brand/country pilot tests identity,access,payroll/time handoffs,service coverage,user feedback and rollback.
[Execution theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/master/theme-e-execution.md)
## Act VI — Prove Value or Change Direction (OVC-M20–22)
Proposed measures include first-time-right payroll,time-to-readiness,digital adoption,case resolution,data quality and service outcomes. All numeric baselines and targets remain TBD.
Source '13/13 journeys curated' describes content curation, not completed implementations. The board scales,redesigns or stops using observed evidence.
[Value theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/master/theme-f-value.md)
## Meet the Fictional Stakeholders
Maya Sterling—CEO; Adrian Tan—CFO; Elena Rossi—Consumer/Brand; Ravi Kapoor—CHRO; Nadia Rahman—Payroll; Oliver Brooks—Store Operations; Lin Chen—Digital Commerce; Sofia Mendes—Acquisition/Onboarding; Aisha Okafor—Learning/Skills; Daniel Weber—Rewards/Performance; Priya Shah—EA; Jonas Lim—Integration/Data; Farah Ahmed—Security/Privacy; Mateo Silva—Supply Chain/Sourcing; Emma Clarke—Customer; Nikhil Das—Associate.
[Persona authority, objections and withheld evidence](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md)
## Practice and Derive
Twelve simulations cover discovery,readiness,funding,connected lifecycle,payroll,rewards,privacy,customer escalation,sourcing,AI,architecture and hypothetical STAR practice.
Seven scope blueprints cover Workforce/HR,CX,Finance,Procurement,Supply Chain,Business Transformation and Leadership. Workforce is source-detailed; other streams require discovery. Gamma,Kahoot,Canva,PPT and LMS media remain planned.
[Scripts](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/simulations/scenario-scripts.md) · [Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [13 HR source links](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/references/notion-child-cases.md)
## Source and Synchronization Governance
Original research stays protected below this boundary. Exact narrative text is mapped to GitHub with per-case revisions and conflict holds. Broader canonical changes require deliberate reconciliation. Child pages and attachments are not losslessly mirrored.
[Sources and gaps](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/references/source-and-assumptions.md) · [Sync protocol](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/sync/README.md) · [Delivery report](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/04-consumer-discretionary/omnivibe-consumer-ltd/delivery-report-2026-10-19.md)
**Delivery validation:** GitHub-to-Notion narrative was read back successfully. This note originated in Notion for the reverse-transfer test. OmniVibe is registered for daily reconciliation; unattended integration remains unverified.

# 🌟 GICS04. **OmniVibe Consumer Ltd. — Digital Transformation Case Study** ## **Company Overview** **OmniVibe Consumer Ltd.** is a fictional multinational consumer-discretionary group operating across fashion, beauty, home, specialty retail, travel experiences, and digital commerce. It represents a modern consumer business balancing brand desirability, omnichannel convenience, responsible sourcing, and profitable growth. --- ## **📊 Company Profile**
**Attribute** **Details**
**Founded** 1992 — 30+ years of consumer-brand operations
**Headquarters** London, UK & Singapore
**Global Presence** 48 countries across 6 continents
**Annual Revenue** \$28 billion USD
**Employees** 72,000 worldwide
**Active Customers** 64 million loyalty members and digital shoppers
### **Business Portfolio**
**Business Segment** **Revenue %** **Operations**
**Fashion & Lifestyle** 32% Apparel, footwear, accessories, premium private labels
**Beauty & Personal Care** 18% Beauty stores, salon partnerships, direct-to-consumer brands
**Home & Living** 17% Furniture, décor, home improvement, marketplace sellers
**Specialty Retail** 15% Electronics, sports, hobby, and experience-led stores
**Travel & Experiences** 10% Boutique hotels, leisure memberships, destination retail
**Digital Marketplace** 8% Third-party merchants, social commerce, retail media
### **Strategic Assets** - **Retail Network:** 3,200 owned and franchise stores - **Digital Ecosystem:** 14 local e-commerce sites, mobile apps, and social-commerce channels - **Fulfillment Footprint:** 26 distribution centers and 140 micro-fulfillment locations - **Supply Network:** 3,800 suppliers and manufacturing partners - **Customer Data:** Unified loyalty, transaction, service, and engagement records --- ## **🎯 Digital Transformation Vision** > *“Delivering inspiring, personalized, and responsible consumer experiences — anywhere, anytime, through one connected brand ecosystem.”* ### **Transformation Drivers** 1. **Omnichannel Expectations** — frictionless discovery, purchase, return, and service across channels 2. **Personalization at Scale** — convert customer insight into relevant experiences and offers 3. **Inventory Productivity** — reduce stock-outs, markdowns, and slow-moving inventory 4. **Brand and Product Innovation** — shorten trend-to-market cycles without compromising quality 5. **Responsible Consumption** — improve product traceability, resale, repair, and sustainable sourcing 6. **Workforce Agility** — build a connected, capable, data-driven workforce that can scale with the consumer ecosystem --- # 👥 **Workforce Monday — 13-Journey Learning Architecture** ## **Workforce Transformation Story** OmniVibe’s consumer transformation depends on a workforce that can operate seamlessly across stores, digital commerce, corporate functions, fulfillment, customer service, and partner ecosystems. **Workforce Monday** therefore becomes the people-architecture backbone of the OmniVibe case study. The 13 journeys are designed as one connected capability chain: **Foundation → Acquire → Onboard → Perform → Develop → Reward → Learn → Pay → Time → Understand → Experience → Augment → Connect.** ### **The 13 OmniVibe Workforce Journeys**
**Code** **Learning Journey** **Workforce Outcome**
**HR01** OmniVibe — Architecting the Consumer Workforce Foundation with SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central A trusted global workforce core and organizational structure
**HR02a** OmniVibe — Architecting Autonomous Talent Acquisition with SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting Faster, skills-aware and data-driven hiring
**HR02b** OmniVibe — Architecting Consumer Onboarding with SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding Consistent digital onboarding from offer to productivity
**HR03** OmniVibe — Architecting High-Performance Consumer Teams with SAP SuccessFactors Performance & Goals Aligned goals, continuous performance and stronger execution
**HR04** OmniVibe — Architecting Leadership and Succession with SAP SuccessFactors Succession & Development Visible talent pipelines and leadership continuity
**HR05** OmniVibe — Architecting Consumer Rewards with SAP SuccessFactors Compensation & Variable Pay Fair, differentiated and business-aligned rewards
**HR06** OmniVibe — Architecting Continuous Consumer Learning with SAP SuccessFactors Learning Skills growth, compliance and capability mobility
**HR07** OmniVibe — Architecting Autonomous Payroll with SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll Accurate, compliant and scalable payroll operations
**HR08** OmniVibe — Architecting Workforce Time and Operations with SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking Optimized attendance, scheduling and workforce operations
**HR09** OmniVibe — Architecting Workforce Intelligence with SAP SuccessFactors People Analytics Evidence-based workforce decisions and executive insight
**HR10** OmniVibe — Architecting Digital Employee Experience with SAP SuccessFactors Work Zone One connected digital front door for employees
**HR11** OmniVibe — Architecting AI-Powered HR with SAP Joule and Intelligent Automation AI-assisted HR productivity and intelligent service delivery
**HR12** OmniVibe — Architecting the Connected HR Enterprise with SAP Integration Suite and SAP BTP Connected HR processes, applications, data and ecosystems
## **Capability Chain** ```plain text FOUNDATION ↓ ATTRACT → ONBOARD → PERFORM → DEVELOP → REWARD → LEARN ↓ PAY → TIME → ANALYZE → EXPERIENCE → AUGMENT → CONNECT Outcome: One Workforce Architecture supporting one connected consumer enterprise ``` ## **Workforce Transformation Outcomes**
**Dimension** **Current State** **OmniVibe Target State**
Workforce Core Country-specific HR structures and duplicate records Global workforce foundation with governed local execution
Talent Recruiting and succession managed in functional silos Skills-aware talent lifecycle from hire to leadership
Performance Annual and inconsistent performance cycles Continuous goals, feedback and outcome alignment
Rewards Fragmented compensation processes Transparent, differentiated and business-linked rewards
Learning Course-centric compliance learning Skills-centric learning and mobility ecosystem
Payroll & Time Manual interventions and fragmented processes Automated, controlled and scalable payroll/time operations
Employee Experience Multiple HR portals and disconnected journeys One digital employee front door with embedded intelligence
AI & Automation Reactive service delivery and repetitive administration AI-assisted self-service, recommendations and workflow automation
Integration Point-to-point interfaces and batch dependencies API-led, event-aware and reusable integration architecture
--- # 🏗️ **TOGAF-Aligned Architecture Design** ## **Phase A: Architecture Vision** ### **Business Context & Stakeholders**
**Stakeholder Group** **Key Concerns** **Success Measures**
**Board & Investors** Profitable growth, brand strength, workforce productivity Improved productivity, retention and operating leverage
**Employees** Easy HR access, career growth, fair rewards, meaningful work Higher digital adoption, engagement and internal mobility
**Store & Service Leaders** Right skills, staffing visibility, performance and scheduling Higher workforce readiness and service productivity
**HR & Payroll** Process control, data quality, compliance and scalability Lower manual effort and stronger data/process governance
**Technology & Enterprise Architecture** Integration, security, extensibility, cost and modernization Reusable architecture and reduced technical complexity
### **Current-State Challenges** #### **Enterprise Level** - Workforce processes vary significantly by country, brand and operating model - Employee, position, organization and skills data are fragmented - Recruiting, onboarding, learning, performance and succession operate as separate journeys - Workforce decisions depend on delayed and inconsistent reporting - Employees navigate multiple disconnected HR experiences #### **Technology Level** - Multiple HR applications with overlapping functionality - Legacy payroll/time integrations create batch dependencies - Point-to-point interfaces increase maintenance effort - AI and automation capabilities are not consistently embedded in HR journeys - Security, privacy and access controls require stronger architectural consistency --- ## **Phase B: Business Architecture** ### **Workforce Value Stream Mapping** ```plain text PLAN WORKFORCE → ATTRACT → ONBOARD → ENABLE → PERFORM → DEVELOP → REWARD → PAY → SCHEDULE → UNDERSTAND → EXPERIENCE → AUGMENT → CONNECT Current State: Fragmented HR processes and channel-specific employee journeys Future State: One connected workforce lifecycle orchestrated around employee and business outcomes ``` ### **Core Workforce Capabilities**
**Capability Domain** **Current Maturity** **Target Maturity** **Digital Enablers**
Core HR Level 2 — Fragmented Level 4 — Governed Employee Central, position management, workflow
Talent Acquisition Level 2 — Process-led Level 4 — Skills-aware Recruiting, automation, talent intelligence
Employee Lifecycle Level 2 — Manual handoffs Level 4 — Digital journey Onboarding, Work Zone, workflow
Performance & Development Level 2 — Annual cycles Level 4 — Continuous Performance & Goals, Succession & Development
Rewards Level 2 — Policy-driven Level 4 — Differentiated Compensation, Variable Pay, analytics
Learning & Skills Level 2 — Course-centric Level 4 — Skills-centric Learning, skills intelligence, mobility
Payroll & Time Level 2 — Transactional Level 4 — Automated Employee Central Payroll, Time Tracking
Workforce Intelligence Level 1 — Reporting Level 4 — Decision intelligence People Analytics, governed metrics
Employee Experience Level 2 — Portal-based Level 4 — Contextual Work Zone, Joule, embedded services
HR Integration Level 1 — Point-to-point Level 4 — Ecosystem-led SAP BTP, Integration Suite, APIs, events
--- ## **Phase C: Information Systems Architecture** ### **Data Architecture**
**Data Domain** **Critical Data** **Quality Requirements** **Governance Model**
Workforce Master Person, employment, organization, position, job Accurate, current, uniquely identified Global HR data governance
Talent & Skills Applications, competencies, goals, performance, potential Trusted, relevant and skills-linked Talent data stewardship
Learning Courses, completions, certifications, skills Complete and auditable Learning governance
Payroll & Time Time, attendance, payroll results, statutory data Accurate, secure and reconciled Payroll and workforce operations governance
People Analytics Headcount, turnover, workforce cost, diversity, mobility Consistent definitions and governed metrics People analytics council
### **Target Application Landscape**
**Application Layer** **Core Systems** **Architecture Pattern**
**Experience Layer** Work Zone, HR services, manager and employee experiences Digital front door, role-aware experiences
**Process Layer** Employee Central, Recruiting, Onboarding, Performance, Succession, Compensation, Learning, Payroll, Time Integrated cloud business processes
**Integration Layer** SAP Integration Suite, APIs, event-driven integration API-first and reusable integration services
**Data & Analytics Layer** People Analytics and enterprise data platforms Governed data products and decision intelligence
**AI Layer** SAP Joule and workflow automation Embedded AI assistance and intelligent orchestration
--- ## **Phase D: Technology Architecture** ### **Cloud-Native Workforce Platform**
**Workload Type** **Deployment Model** **Rationale**
**Core HR & Talent** Cloud SaaS Standardized global capabilities and continuous innovation
**Payroll & Time** Cloud + controlled integration landscape Compliance, resilience and operational control
**Digital Employee Experience** Cloud Anywhere access and contextual employee services
**Integration Platform** SAP BTP Secure API-led and event-aware connectivity
**AI & Automation** Cloud AI services Scalable workforce assistance and workflow augmentation
### **Technology Standards**
**Technology Stack** **Standard Choice** **Strategic Rationale**
**Core HR Platform** SAP SuccessFactors Integrated workforce lifecycle management
**Business Platform** SAP BTP Extension, integration and innovation foundation
**Integration Platform** SAP Integration Suite Reusable, governed enterprise integration
**Employee Experience** SAP SuccessFactors Work Zone Unified digital workforce experience
**AI Assistant** SAP Joule Conversational assistance and embedded intelligence
**Analytics** SAP SuccessFactors People Analytics Workforce insight and decision support
--- # 🤖 **AI & Advanced Analytics Architecture** ### **AI Use Case Portfolio**
**Use Case** **Business Value** **Technical Approach**
Talent Acquisition Copilot Faster hiring decisions and recruiter productivity Joule-enabled assistance and workflow automation
Onboarding Guidance Reduced time-to-productivity and employee friction Contextual digital guidance and automated tasks
Performance Insight Better coaching and outcome alignment People data, goals and AI-assisted recommendations
Skills Intelligence Improved mobility and workforce planning Skills signals, learning data and talent analytics
Manager Self-Service Lower administrative effort Conversational AI with governed HR transactions
Workforce Risk Detection Earlier identification of attrition and capability risks People analytics and predictive patterns
HR Case Automation Faster service resolution and lower HR operations cost Workflow automation, knowledge assistance and orchestration
--- # 🔗 **Integration Architecture** ```plain text OMNIVIBE WORKFORCE ECOSYSTEM Recruiting ─┐ Onboarding ─┤ Core HR ────┤ Talent ─────┤ Learning ───┤ Payroll ────┼──→ SAP BTP / SAP Integration Suite ──→ Enterprise Ecosystem Time ───────┤ Analytics ──┤ Work Zone ──┤ Joule ──────┘ API-led + Event-aware + Secure + Reusable ``` ### **Integration Principles** - **API-led Integration:** reusable services instead of point-to-point dependencies - **Event-aware Architecture:** propagate workforce events where real-time action matters - **Security by Design:** identity, authorization, privacy and auditability across integrations - **Canonical Data:** common workforce semantics across applications - **Loose Coupling:** business applications remain independently evolvable - **Observability:** monitor interface health, business exceptions and reconciliation --- # 📈 **Transformation Roadmap**
**Wave** **Focus** **Priority Journeys** **Primary Outcome**
**Wave 1 — Foundation** Establish the workforce core HR01, HR07, HR08, HR12 Trusted core HR, payroll, time and integration foundation
**Wave 2 — Talent Lifecycle** Connect the employee lifecycle HR02a, HR02b, HR03, HR04 Faster hiring, onboarding, performance and succession
**Wave 3 — Capability & Rewards** Build workforce capability HR05, HR06 Rewards alignment and continuous learning
**Wave 4 — Intelligence & Experience** Make HR insight-led and employee-centric HR09, HR10, HR11 Workforce intelligence, digital experience and AI augmentation
--- # 🎯 **OmniVibe Workforce Monday — Learning Outcome** By completing these **13 journeys**, the learner should be able to move from individual SAP SuccessFactors product knowledge to an **integrated workforce architecture perspective**: understanding business capabilities, application boundaries, data flows, integration patterns, technology choices, AI opportunities and a practical transformation roadmap for a complex consumer enterprise. ## **Architect's Completion Standard**
**Capability** **Foundation-Level Demonstration**
Business Architecture Explain why each workforce capability matters to OmniVibe's operating model
Application Architecture Map the 13 journeys to the SAP SuccessFactors application landscape
Data Architecture Identify critical workforce data domains and governance needs
Integration Architecture Explain how SAP Integration Suite and SAP BTP connect the workforce ecosystem
Technology Architecture Relate cloud, platform and security decisions to workforce outcomes
AI Architecture Identify practical Joule and automation opportunities with human oversight
Transformation Architecture Sequence the 13 journeys into a credible phased roadmap
> **Workforce Monday principle:** *Do not learn 13 products as 13 silos. Architect one connected workforce system.* --- ## ✅ **13 Journeys Curated** **HR01 • HR02a • HR02b • HR03 • HR04 • HR05 • HR06 • HR07 • HR08 • HR09 • HR10 • HR11 • HR12** **Status: 13/13 Workforce Monday journeys curated for OmniVibe. 🚀** HR01 — OmniVibe — Architecting the Consumer Workforce Foundation with SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central HR02a — OmniVibe — Architecting Autonomous Talent Acquisition with SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting HR02b — OmniVibe — Architecting Consumer Onboarding with SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding HR03 — OmniVibe — Architecting High-Performance Consumer Teams with SAP SuccessFactors Performance & Goals HR04 — OmniVibe — Architecting Leadership and Succession with SAP SuccessFactors Succession & Development HR05 — OmniVibe — Architecting Consumer Rewards with SAP SuccessFactors Compensation & Variable Pay HR06 — OmniVibe — Architecting Continuous Consumer Learning with SAP SuccessFactors Learning HR07 — OmniVibe — Architecting Autonomous Payroll with SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll HR08 — OmniVibe — Architecting Workforce Time and Operations with SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking HR09 — OmniVibe — Architecting Workforce Intelligence with SAP SuccessFactors People Analytics HR10 — OmniVibe — Architecting Digital Employee Experience with SAP SuccessFactors Work Zone HR11 — OmniVibe — Architecting AI-Powered HR with SAP Joule and Intelligent Automation HR12 — OmniVibe — Architecting the Connected HR Enterprise with SAP Integration Suite and SAP BTP
